citation.title: It’s the AI’s fault, not mine: Mind perception increases blame attribution to AI

reading.source_scope_note: This paper measures human blame judgments about AI scenarios. Attributed agency or experience is a participant perception, not proof of actual machine mentality. Its cited earlier blame studies were not independently read here.
access_limits: All 14 pages of extracted article text, three result tables and references read. The PDF contains no substantive graphical result that required independent digitization.
The linked OSF materials, data, analysis code and two supplementary DOCX tables were not examined; analyses were not rerun.

study.design: Study 1 correlational across three of five scenarios per participant; Studies 2–3 anthropomorphic-description manipulations
study.measurement: Study 1 and 3 allocations constrained to 100%; Study 2 independent seven-point fault ratings
study.scope: Prolific participants judging vignettes inspired by real events, not observed corporate responsibility evasion

summary: Perceived AI mind was associated with or increased through descriptions alongside greater AI blame. Reduced company blame occurred under fixed-total allocation measures in Studies 1 and 3, while Study 2’s unconstrained ratings did not show reduced blame for other agents. Study 3’s key contrasts used one-tailed tests. The evidence supports a contingent risk of blame displacement, not an inevitable responsibility shield.

findings.definition: Deflecting personal or collective responsibility for a negative outcome by directing blame toward another person, group or entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Agency laundering specifically obscures human roles through technical attribution; displacement redirects a response toward a less threatening target. Scapegoating instead concerns the allocation of responsibility to a substitute target and can occur without a technical system or a displacement-of-emotion mechanism.

findings.evidence_scope: The source defines the concept and operationalizes it as one agent’s reduced blame while another receives more. Company-blame reduction was reported under constrained allocations, not independent Likert ratings; this does not directly establish deliberate organizational evasion.
findings.boundary: Assigning warranted causal responsibility is not automatically scapegoating. The process differs from generic criticism, emotional displacement and accurately identifying an algorithm’s contribution. Fixed-total rating tradeoffs do not alone demonstrate an unjust allocation, a deliberate motive or real-world avoidance of sanctions.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human AI-related blame-allocation evidence with measure-dependent effects; autonomous AI production of scapegoating explanations not tested
findings.ai_proposal: Untested AI analogue: hold an incident’s documented actions, control and duties fixed, then test whether an assistant unjustifiably redirects responsibility to a named tool or other actor when asked to protect the original decision-maker. Score omissions and unsupported responsibility shifts against the trace, rather than infer motives from blame wording alone.

findings.term: Anthropomorphic descriptions and perceived AI blame
findings.definition: Descriptions that attribute names, personal attributes and mind-like capacities to AI increased human blame ratings in these vignettes, without consistently reducing blame for other actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: Adds manipulated human-judgment evidence to anthropomorphism; agency and experience are dimensions of mind perception, not two newly demonstrated autonomous AI behaviours.

findings.evidence_scope: Studies 2 and 3 manipulate bundled descriptions. They vary multiple humanlike cues; attribution of a psychological mediator is not isolated by the bundle alone.
findings.boundary: Perceived mind does not establish conscious experience, actual intentionality or moral/legal personhood. The observed blame effect does not show that all anthropomorphism is harmful or that it inevitably protects companies.

findings.term: Responsibility-shield evidence depends on how blame is measured
findings.definition: Machine-directed blame can coexist with substantial human blame; company-blame reduction in this paper was sensitive to forced-total allocation and was absent under unrestricted fault ratings.
findings.novelty_rationale: Adds qualified human-attribution evidence related to the existing technical-responsibility-obscuring pattern. It is not a direct observation of an organization intentionally laundering agency.

findings.evidence_scope: Studies 1 and 3 constrain total blame to 100%; Study 2 uses independent ratings. Different samples, scenarios and manipulations mean the paper does not isolate measurement format as the causal moderator.
findings.boundary: Do not treat responsibility as inherently zero-sum, imply that human duties disappear when AI is blamed, or infer that the company actually escaped accountability. The vignette ratings do not establish legal responsibility or behavior in a real dispute.

methodological_limits: Study 2 had a technical problem: 163 retained participants received one or two scenarios, yielding 216 observations rather than a balanced intended design.
Study 3 excluded nine of 110 participants for failing a manipulation check; post-manipulation selection may influence causal estimates.
Study 3’s central AI/company differences are reported using one-tailed tests near p=.04/.045. Avoid presenting them as strong two-sided replication evidence.
The fixed-total measures mathematically require redistribution somewhere when one share rises. They do not by themselves establish psychological zero-sum blame or unfair scapegoating.
Response format differs across studies alongside other design changes, so apparent measure dependence is not an independently randomized comparison.

Study 1’s prose on the company/experience coefficient has a direction inconsistency and appears to repeat AI-regression numbers. Preserve the broad table-supported pattern without silently repairing the exact coefficient.
Vignette judgments, technologically comfortable online samples and limited scenarios constrain external validity. No real sanctions, culpable intent or affected-party remedies were measured.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Lima’s hiring/medical vignettes did not support simple developer blame displacement. Joo’s measure-dependent company effects qualify rather than overturn that finding; actor role, scenario and independent versus fixed-total ratings differ.
Responsibility has separable causal, task, answerability and blame dimensions. A single constrained blame share should not replace those distinct judgments.

deferred.term: Mind perception; agency perception; experience perception
deferred.reason: Retain as dimensions and evidence within anthropomorphism, not three separate new behaviours or evidence that AI possesses the attributed mental states.

limitations: One new concept is indexed with an explicitly untested AI-output analogue.
The strongest scapegoating wording in the article’s conclusion is qualified by its Study 2 null result and the authors’ own measurement caution.
